FILE: website/tools/film/README.md
====================================================================================================
# Product film

The film on the home page (`public/video/deep-algorithms-film.mp4`, 1:22). It is made from code so it can be re-cut when the products or the words change: live-action footage carries the world and the threat, and the site's own product pictures carry the answer.

**Structure.** It follows premium enterprise SaaS films: the product is the hero, shown large, simplified and true to the real app. Callouts sit on glass beside it, never inside it. There is one benefit per product, kinetic type carries the story on mute, the pacing is deliberate, and every product chapter uses the same visual system. The whole film is **one story: one bank in Mumbai, one night, five attacks**.
1. **Cold open (silent):** 21:38 IST, a private bank, every system green, then "Before morning, five attacks will begin."
2. **Problem:** most access now belongs to service accounts, cloud keys and AI agents. Attackers log in, and no alert fires.
3. **Brand:** the plate opens with "catches them before they act" and shows the four product lines.
4. **Five chapters**, each a worst case on screen in silence over a heartbeat, then the product stopping it:
   1. **adapID Fraud Prevention.** A customer on a scam call sends ₹2,40,000 to a new payee, and the payment is held (< 80 ms).
   2. **Zenstra AI.** An agent exports customer records, and the action is blocked (4 ms).
   3. **adapID Identity Risk Management (CIRM).** Right password, wrong person, and every session is revoked (1.4 s).
   4. **BotShield AI.** 18,204 bot logins hit, and 6 of 37 exposures are proven and patched.
   5. **ICMS.** The regulator asks, and the evidence package is ready (< 5 min).

   The camera leans into the one row that matters, with a spotlight, and the result lands as one number on glass. A chapter marker (01/05 … 05/05) keeps the viewer oriented.
5. **Resolution:** 09:00, business as usual. "One night. Five attacks. Nothing lost."
6. **Proof, then the ask:** customers and certifications, then the ask over the city, then the lockup with the products, the button and the URL. The voice ends on "Book a demo."

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `script.json` | The narration, line by line. `lead` is the silence before the first line (the cold open plays in it). `text` is what appears on screen and in captions, `say` is what the voice reads (spellings that help pronunciation, such as "Adap-ID"), and `after` is the pause after each line. The long pauses after `brand`, `fraud`, `zenstra`, `cirm` and `botshield` are the silent worst-case beats. |
| `tts.py` | Synthesises the narration with [Kokoro](https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro) (Apache-2.0), voice `af_heart`, one line at a time. Writes `vo.wav` and `timings.json`. |
| `footage.json` | The live-action shots: source URL, the window used (`in`, `dur`) and per-shot `lift`/`sat`. Every clip is free for commercial use without attribution (Pexels and Coverr licences). See `CREDITS.md`. |
| `footage.py` | Downloads each shot, cuts its window and gives all shots one grade (cool shadows, muted saturation, gentle film curve), so footage from different cameras cuts together. Writes 1920×1080 JPEG frames at 30 fps. |
| `mix.py` | Generates the score (soft pads, a pulse from the brand moment on, whooshes, a chime, a closing swell), plus an impact and riser into each worst-case beat on their own bus. Ducks the score under the voice and sets it 18 dB below speech. |
| `captions.py` | Writes the WebVTT captions from `timings.json`. |
| `render.mjs` | Opens `film.html` on the dev server, serves the footage frames as `/clips/…`, and captures every frame at 1920×1080. |
| `src/dev/film/Film.jsx` | The film: each scene is a pure function of time, cut to `timings.json`. Shots get a slow camera move, grain and lens falloff. The five chapters are one table (`CHAPTERS`): worst case, product picture, focus ring (measured from the DOM), headline and outcome. The product pictures are the site's own, with their steps driven by the film clock. |

## Remake it

```bash
# 1. voice (Python 3.11+): pip install kokoro-onnx soundfile
#    model files: kokoro-v1.0.onnx and voices-v1.0.bin from github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx/releases
python tools/film/tts.py <model-dir> build/film            # vo.wav + timings.json
cp build/film/timings.json tools/film/timings.json

# 2. footage (ffmpeg, curl)
python tools/film/footage.py build/film/cache build/film/clips

# 3. sound
python tools/film/mix.py build/film/vo.wav tools/film/timings.json build/film/mix.wav 82.01

# 4. captions
python tools/film/captions.py tools/film/timings.json public/video/deep-algorithms-film.vtt

# 5. picture (Playwright with Chromium; set CHROMIUM=/path/to/chrome to use a system browser)
npm run dev &                                              # serves film.html
node tools/film/render.mjs http://localhost:5173 build/film/frames build/film/clips

# 6. encode (loudness to -16 LUFS, true peak -1.5 dB)
ffmpeg -framerate 30 -i build/film/frames/f%05d.jpg -i build/film/mix.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a \
  -af "loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=9" -ar 48000 -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 20 -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -profile:v high -level 4.1 -g 60 -movflags +faststart -c:a aac -b:a 160k -shortest \
  public/video/deep-algorithms-film.mp4
ffmpeg -i public/video/deep-algorithms-film.mp4 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 34 -row-mt 1 -c:a libopus -b:a 128k \
  public/video/deep-algorithms-film.webm
ffmpeg -ss 28.6 -i public/video/deep-algorithms-film.mp4 -frames:v 1 -c:v libwebp -quality 86 public/video/film-poster.webp
```

Don't edit source files while `render.mjs` runs. The dev server reloads the page, and the renderer reopens it and redoes the frame, which costs time.

Check the narration by ear, or with a speech-to-text pass (for example faster-whisper `small.en`): every product name should come back spelled correctly. A professional voice recording can replace `vo.wav` one-for-one. If you do, re-time `timings.json` by hand so the scenes stay on the words. Swapping a shot means changing its `src`/`in` in `footage.json` and re-running steps 2 and 5.

FILE: website/tools/film/captions.py

"""WebVTT captions from timings.json. Long lines are split into two cues, at a
full stop if there is one (the one nearest the middle), else at the comma or full stop nearest
the middle; each cue is timed by its share of the words.
Usage: python captions.py timings.json out.vtt"""
import json, re, sys
T = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
def ts(s):
    h, m = int(s // 3600), int(s % 3600 // 60)
    return f'{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s % 60:06.3f}'
out = ['WEBVTT', '']
lines = T['lines']
for li, ln in enumerate(lines):
    text, a, b = ln['text'], ln['start'], ln['end']
    nxt = lines[li + 1]['start'] - 0.05 if li + 1 < len(lines) else b + 1.5
    parts = [text]
    if len(text) > 58:
        # a sentence end near the middle beats a comma at the middle
        stops = [m.end() for m in re.finditer(r'\. ', text) if 0.15 < m.end() / len(text) < 0.85]
        cut = stops or [m.end() for m in re.finditer(r'[.,] ', text)]
        if cut:
            mid = min(cut, key=lambda c: abs(c - len(text) / 2))
            parts = [text[:mid].strip(), text[mid:].strip()]
    words = [len(p.split()) for p in parts]; total = sum(words); t = a
    for j, (p, w) in enumerate(zip(parts, words)):
        e = t + (b - a) * w / total
        end = min(e + 0.4, nxt) if j == len(parts) - 1 else e
        out += [f'{ts(t)} --> {ts(end)}', p, '']
        t = e
open(sys.argv[2], 'w').write('\n'.join(out))
print(open(sys.argv[2]).read())

====================================================================================================
FILE: website/tools/film/footage.py
====================================================================================================
"""Live-action footage for the product film: download each clip in footage.json,
cut its window, give every shot the same grade and write 1920x1080 frames at 30 fps
to <out>/<id>/0001.jpg... render.mjs serves them to film.html as /clips/<id>/NNNN.jpg.
Grade: open shadows, cool shadows, warm-neutral highlights, muted saturation,
so footage from different cameras cuts together and the product colours stay the
only saturated thing on screen.
Usage: python footage.py <cache-dir> <out-dir>"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
cache, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
for c in json.load(open(os.path.join(here, 'footage.json')))['clips']:
    src = os.path.join(cache, c['id'] + '.mp4')
    if not os.path.exists(src):
        subprocess.run(['curl', '-sSfL', '-o', src, c['src']], check=True)
    d = os.path.join(out, c['id']); os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    for f in os.listdir(d): os.remove(os.path.join(d, f))
    lift = c.get('lift', 0)
    vf = ','.join([
        'fps=30', 'scale=1920:1080:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase:flags=lanczos', 'crop=1920:1080',
        f'eq=contrast=1.05:brightness={lift + 0.035:.3f}:saturation={c.get("sat", 0.82)}:gamma=1.06',
        'colorbalance=rs=-0.05:gs=-0.01:bs=0.06:rm=-0.02:bm=0.025:rh=0.02:gh=0.005:bh=-0.02',
        'curves=all=0/0.03 0.25/0.26 0.5/0.54 0.8/0.85 1/0.98',
    ])
    subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-loglevel', 'error', '-y', '-ss', str(c['in']), '-t', str(c['dur']), '-i', src,
                    '-vf', vf, '-q:v', '2', os.path.join(d, '%04d.jpg')], check=True)
    print(c['id'], len(os.listdir(d)), 'frames')

====================================================================================================
FILE: website/tools/film/mix.py
====================================================================================================
"""Sound for the product film: narration over a quiet generated score.
- Score: a slow progression of soft, detuned pads (Dmaj9, Bm11, Gmaj9, A6sus2)
  with a sub bass; a gentle eighth-note pulse joins when the brand appears.
- Accents: airy whooshes on scene changes, a chime on the brand reveal, a low
  impact with a short riser into each worst-case beat (the silent incident before
  every product line) and a low swell under the closing card.
- The score ducks under the voice. Output is 48 kHz stereo WAV; loudness is
  normalised afterwards with ffmpeg (see README).
Usage: python mix.py <vo.wav> <timings.json> <out.wav> [length_seconds]"""
import json, sys
import numpy as np, soundfile as sf

vo_path, tim_path, out_path = sys.argv[1:4]
T = json.load(open(tim_path))
SR = 48000
L = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else T['duration'] + 2.2
N = int(L * SR)
t = np.arange(N) / SR
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
cue = {c['id']: c for c in T['lines']}

def fft_filter(x, lo=None, hi=None, slope=1.0):
    X = np.fft.rfft(x); f = np.fft.rfftfreq(len(x), 1 / SR); g = np.ones_like(f)
    if hi: g *= 1 / np.sqrt(1 + (f / hi) ** (4 * slope))
    if lo: g *= 1 / np.sqrt(1 + (lo / np.maximum(f, 1e-3)) ** (4 * slope))
    return np.fft.irfft(X * g, len(x))

def env_adsr(n, a, r):
    e = np.ones(n); na = min(int(a * SR), n // 2); nr = min(int(r * SR), n - na)
    e[:na] = np.linspace(0, 1, na) ** 2; e[-nr:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, nr) ** 2
    return e

# ---------- voice ----------
v, vsr = sf.read(vo_path, dtype='float32')
if vsr != SR: v = np.interp(np.linspace(0, len(v) - 1, int(len(v) * SR / vsr)), np.arange(len(v)), v).astype(np.float32)
voice = np.zeros(N); voice[:min(N, len(v))] = v[:N]
voice = fft_filter(voice, lo=85, slope=1.0)
# gentle presence lift around 3 kHz, done as a broad parallel band
voice = voice + 0.18 * fft_filter(voice, lo=2200, hi=5200)
# soft knee compression (envelope follower on 10 ms blocks)
blk = int(0.01 * SR); nb = N // blk
rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(voice[:nb * blk].reshape(nb, blk) ** 2, 1) + 1e-9)
thr = np.percentile(rms[rms > 1e-3], 70) if np.any(rms > 1e-3) else 0.1
gain_b = np.where(rms > thr, (thr / rms) ** 0.35, 1.0)
gain = np.repeat(gain_b, blk); gain = np.pad(gain, (0, N - len(gain)), constant_values=1.0)
gain = np.convolve(gain, np.ones(480) / 480, mode='same')
voice *= gain
voice /= np.max(np.abs(voice)) + 1e-9

# ---------- score ----------
def note(freq, start, dur, amp, detune=0.12, bright=1400, attack=1.6, release=2.2):
    s, n = int(start * SR), int(dur * SR)
    if s >= N: return
    n = min(n, N - s); tt = np.arange(n) / SR
    w = np.zeros(n)
    for d in (-detune, 0, detune):
        f = freq * 2 ** (d / 12)
        ph = rng.random() * 2 * np.pi
        # soft saw from a few harmonics
        for h in range(1, 7): w += np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * h * tt + ph * h) / (h ** 1.35)
    w = fft_filter(w, hi=bright, slope=0.8) * env_adsr(n, attack, release) * amp
    score_l[s:s + n] += w * 0.9; score_r[s:s + n] += w * 1.0

score_l = np.zeros(N); score_r = np.zeros(N)
hz = lambda m: 440 * 2 ** ((m - 69) / 12)
CH = [  # midi notes
    [50, 57, 62, 64, 66, 69],      # Dmaj9 (D A D E F# A)
    [47, 54, 59, 62, 64, 69],      # Bm11
    [43, 50, 57, 59, 62, 66],      # Gmaj9
    [45, 52, 57, 59, 64, 66],      # A6sus2
]
bar = 7.4
i = 0; start = 0.0
while start < L:
    ch = CH[i % 4]
    for k, m in enumerate(ch):
        a = 0.05 if k == 0 else 0.022
        note(hz(m), start, bar + 2.4, a, bright=900 if k == 0 else 1600, attack=2.2, release=2.6)
    note(hz(ch[0] - 12), start, bar + 1.5, 0.06, detune=0.0, bright=220, attack=1.2, release=1.8)
    start += bar; i += 1

# eighth-note pulse from the brand moment to the end card
pulse_s, pulse_e = cue['brand']['start'] - 0.4, cue['cta']['start'] + 0.2
eighth = 60 / 96 / 2
p = pulse_s
while p < pulse_e:
    bar_i = int(p // bar) % 4
    m = CH[bar_i][3] + 12
    n = int(0.22 * SR); s = int(p * SR)
    if s + n < N:
        tt = np.arange(n) / SR
        w = np.sin(2 * np.pi * hz(m) * tt) * np.exp(-tt * 18) + 0.3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * hz(m) * 2 * tt) * np.exp(-tt * 26)
        lvl = 0.016 * min(1, (p - pulse_s) / 2.5) * min(1, (pulse_e - p) / 1.5)
        pan = 0.7 if int(p / eighth) % 2 else 0.3
        score_l[s:s + n] += w * lvl * (1 - pan) * 2; score_r[s:s + n] += w * lvl * pan * 2
    p += eighth

# ---------- accents ----------
def whoosh(at, dur=1.1, amp=0.05):
    s, n = int((at - dur * 0.7) * SR), int(dur * SR)
    if s < 0: n += s; s = 0
    x = rng.standard_normal(n)
    low, high = fft_filter(x, lo=250, hi=1100, slope=0.7), fft_filter(x, lo=1800, hi=7500, slope=0.7)
    sweep = np.linspace(0, 1, n) ** 1.5
    out = low / (np.std(low) + 1e-9) * (1 - sweep) + high / (np.std(high) + 1e-9) * sweep * 0.7
    e = np.sin(np.linspace(0, np.pi, n)) ** 2
    w = out * e * amp
    score_l[s:s + n] += w * (0.6 + 0.4 * sweep); score_r[s:s + n] += w * (1.0 - 0.4 * sweep)

def chime(at, amp=0.05):
    for m, a, dec in ((86, 1.0, 1.4), (93, 0.55, 1.8), (98, 0.35, 2.2), (74, 0.5, 2.6)):
        n = int(3.2 * SR); s = int(at * SR); tt = np.arange(n) / SR
        w = (np.sin(2 * np.pi * hz(m) * tt) + 0.2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * hz(m) * 2.01 * tt)) * np.exp(-tt * dec) * a * amp
        w *= np.minimum(1, tt / 0.004)
        score_l[s:s + n] += w; score_r[s:s + n] += w * 0.92

def swell(at, dur=3.5, amp=0.08):
    n = int(dur * SR); s = int(at * SR); tt = np.arange(n) / SR
    w = sum(np.sin(2 * np.pi * hz(m) * tt) / (1 + j) for j, m in enumerate((38, 50, 57)))
    w *= np.sin(np.linspace(0, np.pi, n)) ** 1.5 * amp
    score_l[s:s + n] += w; score_r[s:s + n] += w

fx_l = np.zeros(N); fx_r = np.zeros(N)  # impacts sit on their own bus, set against the voice, not the score

def impact(at, amp=0.16):
    # sub drop + filtered noise thump + a dry tick: the moment a worst case appears
    n = int(2.6 * SR); s = int(at * SR)
    if s + n > N: n = N - s
    tt = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 46 * np.exp(-tt * 1.6) + 30
    sub = np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR) * np.exp(-tt * 1.9)
    thump = fft_filter(rng.standard_normal(n), hi=380, slope=1.0); thump = thump / (np.std(thump) + 1e-9) * np.exp(-tt * 9) * 0.35
    tick = fft_filter(rng.standard_normal(n), lo=2500, hi=9000, slope=0.8); tick = tick / (np.std(tick) + 1e-9) * np.exp(-tt * 60) * 0.12
    w = (sub + thump + tick) * amp * np.minimum(1, tt / 0.003)
    fx_l[s:s + n] += w; fx_r[s:s + n] += w

def riser(end, dur=0.9, amp=0.03):
    n = int(dur * SR); s = int((end - dur) * SR); tt = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = fft_filter(rng.standard_normal(n), lo=900, hi=6000, slope=0.7); x /= np.std(x) + 1e-9
    w = x * (tt / dur) ** 2.2 * amp
    fx_l[s:s + n] += w * 0.9; fx_r[s:s + n] += w

def pulse(a, b, bpm=96, amp=0.09):
    # a low heartbeat under a worst-case beat: tension without music
    beat = 60 / bpm; p = a + beat
    while p < b - 0.1:
        for off, g in ((0, 1.0), (0.18, 0.6)):
            n = int(0.35 * SR); s = int((p + off) * SR)
            if s + n > N: break
            tt = np.arange(n) / SR
            w = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 52 * tt) * np.exp(-tt * 14) * g * amp
            fx_l[s:s + n] += w; fx_r[s:s + n] += w
        p += beat

# worst-case beats: they start just after the line before them ends (Film.jsx: inc1..inc4)
CHAP = [k for k in ('fraud', 'zenstra', 'cirm', 'botshield', 'icms') if k in cue]  # Film.jsx CHAPTERS, in order
INC = [(cue['brand']['end'] + 0.8 if i == 0 else cue[CHAP[i - 1]]['end'] + 0.25, k) for i, k in enumerate(CHAP)]
for a0, k in INC:
    pulse(a0, cue[k]['start'] + 0.6)
for at, _ in INC:
    riser(at); impact(at)
impact(0.45, amp=0.12)  # cold open: the night begins
if 'recap' in cue: chime(cue['recap']['start'] - 0.4, amp=0.045)  # the morning after
for k in ('shift', 'login', 'trust'):
    whoosh(cue[k]['start'] - 0.15, amp=0.035)
for k in CHAP:  # into each product: the answer arrives
    whoosh(cue[k]['start'] + 0.6, dur=0.8, amp=0.04)
chime(cue['brand']['start'] - 0.25, amp=0.06)
whoosh(cue['brand']['start'] - 0.3, dur=1.6, amp=0.05)
swell(cue['cta']['start'] - 0.6, dur=6.5, amp=0.06)

# ---------- duck the score under the voice ----------
ve = np.abs(voice)
k = int(0.05 * SR)
ve = np.convolve(ve, np.ones(k) / k, mode='same')
att = np.convolve(ve > 0.02, np.ones(int(0.25 * SR)) / int(0.25 * SR), mode='same')
duck = 1 - 0.5 * np.clip(att, 0, 1)
score = np.stack([score_l, score_r], 1) * duck[:, None]

# fades
fade = np.clip(t / 1.2, 0, 1) * np.clip((L - t) / 2.0, 0, 1)
score *= fade[:, None]

# level the score against the voice: 18 dB under it while she speaks
speaking = att > 0.5
v_rms = np.sqrt(np.mean((voice[speaking] * 0.62) ** 2))
s_rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(score[speaking] ** 2))
score *= (v_rms / s_rms) * 10 ** (-18 / 20)
fx = np.stack([fx_l, fx_r], 1)
fx *= (np.max(np.abs(voice)) * 0.62 * 0.7) / (np.max(np.abs(fx)) + 1e-9)  # impacts peak 3 dB under the voice
mix = voice[:, None] * 0.62 + score + fx
mix /= max(1.0, np.max(np.abs(mix)) / 0.95)
sf.write(out_path, mix.astype(np.float32), SR, subtype='PCM_24')
s2 = np.sqrt(np.mean(score[speaking] ** 2)); gaps = np.sqrt(np.mean(score[~speaking] ** 2))
print(f'length {L:.2f}s  voice {20*np.log10(v_rms):.1f} dBFS  score under voice {20*np.log10(s2):.1f} dBFS  score in gaps {20*np.log10(gaps):.1f} dBFS  peak {20*np.log10(np.max(np.abs(mix))):.1f} dBFS')

// Renders the product film frame by frame from the dev server's film.html.
// node tools/film/render.mjs <base-url> <frames-dir> <clips-dir> [from] [to]
// <clips-dir> holds the graded footage frames written by footage.py; they are
// served to the page as /clips/<id>/NNNN.jpg. Requires `npm run dev` and Playwright's Chromium.
import { chromium } from 'playwright';
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
const [, , base = 'http://localhost:5173', out = 'frames', clips = 'build/film/clips', from, to] = process.argv;
mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
const b = await chromium.launch(process.env.CHROMIUM ? { executablePath: process.env.CHROMIUM } : {});
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1920, height: 1080 }, deviceScaleFactor: 1 });
const errs = []; p.on('pageerror', (e) => errs.push(String(e)));
await p.route('**/clips/**', (r) => {
  const rel = new URL(r.request().url()).pathname.replace(/^\/clips\//, '');
  try { r.fulfill({ body: readFileSync(join(clips, rel)), contentType: 'image/jpeg', headers: { 'cache-control': 'max-age=3600' } }); }
  catch { r.fulfill({ status: 404, body: '' }); }
});
const open = async () => { await p.goto(`${base}/film.html`, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' }); await p.waitForTimeout(1000); };
await open();
const { L, F } = await p.evaluate(() => ({ L: window.__LENGTH, F: window.__FPS }));
const n = Math.round(L * F), i0 = from ? +from : 0, i1 = to ? Math.min(+to, n) : n;
const t0 = Date.now();
for (let i = i0; i < i1; i++) {
  // the dev server reloads the page if a source file changes mid-render: reopen and redo the frame
  try { await p.evaluate((t) => window.__film(t), i / F); } catch { await open(); await p.evaluate((t) => window.__film(t), i / F); }
  await p.screenshot({ path: `${out}/f${String(i).padStart(5, '0')}.jpg`, type: 'jpeg', quality: 93 });
  if (i % 150 === 0) console.log(`frame ${i}/${n}  ${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(0)} s`);
}
if (errs.length) console.log('ERRORS', errs.slice(0, 5));
await b.close();

FILE: website/tools/film/tts.py
====================================================================================================
"""Narration for the product film: one Kokoro voice, one sentence at a time.
Writes <out>/vo.wav and <out>/timings.json (start and end of every line, seconds).
A line may carry "soften": [from_s, to_s, dB] to bring one stressed word level with the rest.
Usage: python tts.py <kokoro-model-dir> <out-dir> [voice] [speed]"""
import json, sys, os
import numpy as np, soundfile as sf
from kokoro_onnx import Kokoro

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
spec = json.load(open(os.path.join(here, 'script.json')))
mdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
voice = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else spec['voice']
speed = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else spec['speed']
k = Kokoro(os.path.join(mdir, 'kokoro-v1.0.onnx'), os.path.join(mdir, 'voices-v1.0.bin'))

def trim(a, sr, thr=0.008):
    idx = np.where(np.abs(a) > thr)[0]
    if not len(idx): return a
    s, e = max(0, idx[0] - int(0.02 * sr)), min(len(a), idx[-1] + int(0.06 * sr))
    return a[s:e]

lead = spec.get('lead', 0.6)  # silence before the first line: the cold open plays here
parts, t, cues, sr = [], lead, [], 24000
for ln in spec['lines']:
    a, sr = k.create(ln['say'], voice=voice, speed=speed, lang='en-us')
    a = trim(a.astype(np.float32), sr)
    if 'soften' in ln:  # [from_s, to_s, dB]: level a word down smoothly, e.g. a name the voice leans on
        s0, s1, db = ln['soften']; g = np.ones(len(a), np.float32); lo = 10 ** (db / 20)
        i0, i1, ramp = int(s0 * sr), min(len(a), int(s1 * sr)), int(0.12 * sr)
        g[i0:i1] = lo; g[i1:i1 + ramp] = np.linspace(lo, 1, len(g[i1:i1 + ramp]))
        a *= g
    fade = int(0.012 * sr); a[:fade] *= np.linspace(0, 1, fade); a[-fade:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, fade)
    d = len(a) / sr
    cues.append({'id': ln['id'], 'text': ln['text'], 'start': round(t, 3), 'end': round(t + d, 3)})
    parts.append(a); t += d
    gap = ln.get('after', 0.5); parts.append(np.zeros(int(gap * sr), np.float32)); t += gap
pcm = np.concatenate([np.zeros(int(lead * sr), np.float32)] + parts)
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
sf.write(os.path.join(out, 'vo.wav'), pcm, sr, subtype='PCM_16')
json.dump({'duration': round(t, 3), 'voice': voice, 'speed': speed, 'lines': cues}, open(os.path.join(out, 'timings.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
print(voice, speed, 'total', round(t, 2), 's,', sum(len(l['text'].split()) for l in spec['lines']), 'words')

// Writes src/components/scenes/land.json: Natural Earth land (public domain, via
// the world-atlas package) sampled on a near-equal-area grid, as a flat array
// [lat*10, lon*10, ...] for the dotted globe. Needs three packages that the site
// itself does not:  npm i --no-save world-atlas@2 d3-geo@3 topojson-client@3
//   node tools/scenes/gen-land.mjs src/components/scenes/land.json 1.8
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { feature } from 'topojson-client';
import { geoContains } from 'd3-geo';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const topo = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(require.resolve('world-atlas/land-50m.json')));
const land = feature(topo, topo.objects.land);
const step = +(process.argv[3] || 2);
const out = [];
for (let lat = -58; lat <= 80; lat += step) {
  const dl = step / Math.max(0.2, Math.cos((lat * Math.PI) / 180));
  for (let lon = -180; lon < 180; lon += dl) if (geoContains(land, [lon, lat])) out.push(Math.round(lat * 10), Math.round(lon * 10));
}
fs.writeFileSync(process.argv[2], JSON.stringify(out));
console.log('dots', out.length / 2);

FILE: website/tools/walkthrough/clock.js
====================================================================================================
/* Injected before any page script. Replaces the page's clocks (performance.now,
   Date.now, requestAnimationFrame, timers) with a virtual clock that only moves
   when the recorder calls window.__frame(dt), and steps every CSS animation,
   transition and SVG (SMIL) animation to that clock. Each recorded frame is therefore exact, however long
   the screenshot takes. Scroll-driven animations keep their scroll timeline. */
(() => {
  const realSetTimeout = window.setTimeout.bind(window);
  const t0 = Date.now();
  let vt = 0;
  performance.now = () => vt;
  Date.now = () => t0 + vt;

  let raf = new Map(), rafId = 0;
  window.requestAnimationFrame = (cb) => { raf.set(++rafId, cb); return rafId; };
  window.cancelAnimationFrame = (id) => { raf.delete(id); };

  const timers = new Map(); let tid = 0;
  window.setTimeout = (cb, ms = 0, ...a) => { timers.set(++tid, { at: vt + Math.max(0, +ms || 0), cb, a }); return tid; };
  window.setInterval = (cb, ms = 0, ...a) => { const every = Math.max(1, +ms || 0); timers.set(++tid, { at: vt + every, cb, a, every }); return tid; };
  window.clearTimeout = window.clearInterval = (id) => { timers.delete(id); };

  const start = new WeakMap(), ours = new WeakSet();
  const tick = () => new Promise((r) => realSetTimeout(r, 4));

  function runTimers(end) {
    for (let guard = 0; guard < 10000; guard++) {
      let next = null, nid = 0;
      for (const [id, t] of timers) if (t.at <= end && (!next || t.at < next.at)) { next = t; nid = id; }
      if (!next) break;
      vt = Math.max(vt, next.at);
      if (next.every) next.at += next.every; else timers.delete(nid);
      try { typeof next.cb === 'function' ? next.cb(...next.a) : 0; } catch (e) { console.error(e); }
    }
    vt = end;
  }
  function stepAnimations() {
    for (const a of document.getAnimations()) {
      if (a.timeline && a.timeline !== document.timeline) continue; // scroll-driven
      if (!start.has(a)) {
        if (a.playState === 'paused' && !ours.has(a)) continue; // paused by the page (e.g. hover)
        start.set(a, vt); // starts on the next recorded frame, however long loading took
      }
      if (a.playState === 'paused' && !ours.has(a)) continue;
      if (a.playState === 'finished') continue;
      a.pause(); ours.add(a);
      a.currentTime = vt - start.get(a);
    }
    // SVG (SMIL) motion: particles along graph edges run on each <svg>'s own clock
    for (const svg of document.querySelectorAll('svg')) {
      if (svg.ownerSVGElement || !svg.querySelector('animate, animateMotion, animateTransform')) continue;
      svg.pauseAnimations(); svg.setCurrentTime(vt / 1000);
    }
  }
  window.__vt = () => vt;
  /* move the clock without recording (while a page or chunk loads) */
  window.__idle = (dt) => { runTimers(vt + dt); const q = raf; raf = new Map(); q.forEach((cb) => { try { cb(vt); } catch (e) { console.error(e); } }); };
  /* advance dt ms; optionally scroll first so scroll handlers see the new position */
  window.__frame = async (dt, scrollY) => {
    runTimers(vt + dt);
    if (scrollY != null && Math.abs(window.scrollY - scrollY) > 0.1) {
      window.scrollTo({ top: scrollY, left: 0, behavior: 'instant' });
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event('scroll'));
    }
    const q = raf; raf = new Map();
    q.forEach((cb) => { try { cb(vt); } catch (e) { console.error(e); } });
    await tick(); await tick();   // let React commit what the timers and frames scheduled
    stepAnimations();
    return vt;
  };
})();

FILE: website/tools/walkthrough/make-video.sh
====================================================================================================
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Joins the recorded segments into one MP4 with chapters.
#   tools/walkthrough/make-video.sh <frames-dir> <out.mp4>
# Each segment is a folder of f00000.jpg… frames plus chapters.json (record.mjs);
# intro.png and devices.png come from cards.mjs.
set -euo pipefail
F=${1:-walkthrough-frames}; OUT=${2:-walkthrough.mp4}
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
FPS=30; XF=0.5
ORDER=$(node -e "import('$HERE/script.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.ORDER.join(' ')))")
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
enc() { ffmpeg -loglevel error -y "$@" -c:v libx264 -preset medium -crf 14 -pix_fmt yuv420p -r $FPS "$TMP/$SEG.mp4"; }

# intro card: 3.5 s, fades in from black
SEG=intro; enc -loop 1 -t 3.5 -framerate $FPS -i "$F/intro.png" -vf "fade=in:0:20"
LIST=(intro)
for SEG in $ORDER; do
  if [ "$SEG" = devices ]; then
    # phone (780x1688 frames) and tablet (820x1180) side by side on the backdrop
    enc -loop 1 -framerate $FPS -i "$F/devices.png" -framerate $FPS -i "$F/phone/f%05d.jpg" -framerate $FPS -i "$F/tablet/f%05d.jpg" -filter_complex \
      "[1]scale=-2:900,pad=iw+16:ih+16:8:8:color=0x2a3446[ph];[2]scale=-2:900,pad=iw+16:ih+16:8:8:color=0x2a3446[tb];[0][ph]overlay=300+(444-overlay_w)/2:84:shortest=1[a];[a][tb]overlay=880+(740-overlay_w)/2:84:shortest=1"
  else
    enc -framerate $FPS -i "$F/$SEG/f%05d.jpg"
  fi
  LIST+=("$SEG")
done

# join with short cross-fades, and write chapters
INPUTS=(); FILTER=""; PREV="[0:v]"; OFF=0; META="$TMP/meta.txt"
echo ";FFMETADATA1" > "$META"; : > "${OUT%.mp4}-chapters.txt"
for i in "${!LIST[@]}"; do
  INPUTS+=(-i "$TMP/${LIST[$i]}.mp4")
  D=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 "$TMP/${LIST[$i]}.mp4")
  START=$OFF
  node -e "
    const fs=require('fs');const seg='${LIST[$i]}',start=$START,d=$D;
    let ch=[];try{ch=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('$F/'+seg+'/chapters.json')).chapters}catch{}
    if(seg==='intro')ch=[{t:0,text:'Introduction'}]; if(seg==='devices')ch=[{t:0,text:'Phone and tablet'}];
    const fmt=(s)=>{s=Math.round(s);return Math.floor(s/60)+':'+String(s%60).padStart(2,'0')};
    ch.forEach((c,k)=>{const a=start+c.t,b=k+1<ch.length?start+ch[k+1].t:start+d-$XF;
      fs.appendFileSync('$META','[CHAPTER]\nTIMEBASE=1/1000\nSTART='+Math.round(a*1000)+'\nEND='+Math.round(b*1000)+'\ntitle='+c.text+(c.sub?' — '+c.sub:'')+'\n');
      fs.appendFileSync('${OUT%.mp4}-chapters.txt',fmt(a)+'  '+c.text+(c.sub?' — '+c.sub:'')+'\n');});"
  if [ "$i" -gt 0 ]; then
    FILTER+="${PREV}[$i:v]xfade=transition=fade:duration=$XF:offset=$(node -e "console.log(($OFF).toFixed(3))")[v$i];"
    PREV="[v$i]"
  fi
  OFF=$(node -e "console.log($OFF + $D - $XF)")
done
ffmpeg -loglevel error -y "${INPUTS[@]}" -i "$META" -filter_complex "${FILTER%;}" -map "$PREV" -map_metadata ${#LIST[@]} -map_chapters ${#LIST[@]} \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 20 -tune animation -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart "$OUT"
rm -rf "$TMP"
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration,size -of default=nw=1 "$OUT"

====================================================================================================
FILE: website/tools/walkthrough/record.mjs
====================================================================================================
// Records the site walkthrough, frame by frame, on a virtual clock (clock.js).
// node tools/walkthrough/record.mjs <base-url> <out-dir> <segment> [width height]
// Serve a production build first: npm run build && npm run serve.
import { chromium } from 'playwright';
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { SEGMENTS } from './script.mjs';

const [, , base = 'http://localhost:4173', outRoot = 'walkthrough-frames', name, W = '1920', H = '1080', dpr = '1'] = process.argv;
const FPS = 30, DT = 1000 / FPS;
const out = `${outRoot}/${name}`; mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
const clock = readFileSync(new URL('./clock.js', import.meta.url), 'utf8');

const OVERLAY = `(() => {
  if (document.getElementById('__cur')) return;
  const s = document.createElement('style');
  s.textContent = '#__cur{position:fixed;left:0;top:0;z-index:2147483647;pointer-events:none;width:26px;height:26px;filter:drop-shadow(0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.45));will-change:transform}'
   + '#__rip{position:fixed;left:0;top:0;z-index:2147483646;pointer-events:none;width:44px;height:44px;margin:-22px 0 0 -22px;border-radius:50%;border:2px solid rgba(0,174,239,.9);background:rgba(0,174,239,.18);opacity:0}'
   + '#__lab{position:fixed;left:32px;bottom:30px;z-index:2147483645;pointer-events:none;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;padding:10px 18px 10px 14px;border-radius:999px;background:rgba(6,10,18,.82);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.16);color:#fff;font:600 17px/1.2 "Inter Variable",system-ui,sans-serif;letter-spacing:-.01em;opacity:0;box-shadow:0 12px 30px -12px rgba(0,0,0,.6)}'
   + '#__lab i{width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:50%;background:#27b8f2;box-shadow:0 0 10px #27b8f2}#__lab small{font-weight:500;color:rgba(255,255,255,.62);font-size:14px}';
  document.documentElement.appendChild(s);
  const c = document.createElement('div'); c.id = '__cur';
  c.innerHTML = '<svg viewBox="0 0 26 26" width="26" height="26"><path d="M5 3.5v17.2l4.6-4.3 2.9 6.6 3-1.3-2.9-6.5h6.3z" fill="#fff" stroke="#0a1526" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>';
  const r = document.createElement('div'); r.id = '__rip';
  const l = document.createElement('div'); l.id = '__lab'; l.innerHTML = '<i></i><span></span><small></small>';
  document.documentElement.append(c, r, l);
})()`;

const b = await chromium.launch();
const ctx = await b.newContext({ viewport: { width: +W, height: +H }, deviceScaleFactor: +dpr, isMobile: +W < 900, hasTouch: +W < 900, reducedMotion: 'no-preference' });
await ctx.addInitScript(clock);
const p = await ctx.newPage();
const errs = []; p.on('pageerror', (e) => errs.push(String(e)));

const ease = (t) => (t < 0.5 ? 4 * t * t * t : 1 - Math.pow(-2 * t + 2, 3) / 2);
let frame = 0, y = 0, cur = { x: +W * 0.62, y: +H * 0.55 }, rip = -1, lab = { text: '', sub: '', at: -1, until: -1 };
const chapters = [];

async function shoot() {
  const f = frame;
  const ripT = rip < 0 ? -1 : (f - rip) / (FPS * 0.45);
  const labA = lab.at < 0 ? 0 : Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (f - lab.at) / (FPS * 0.35), (lab.until - f) / (FPS * 0.5)));
  await p.evaluate(async ([dt, sy, cx, cy, rt, la, lt, ls]) => {
    await window.__frame(dt, sy);
    const c = document.getElementById('__cur'); if (c) c.style.transform = `translate(${cx - 5}px, ${cy - 3}px)`;
    const r = document.getElementById('__rip');
    if (r) { if (rt >= 0 && rt <= 1) { r.style.opacity = String(0.9 * (1 - rt)); r.style.transform = `translate(${cx}px, ${cy}px) scale(${0.3 + rt * 0.9})`; } else r.style.opacity = '0'; }
    const l = document.getElementById('__lab');
    if (l) { l.style.opacity = String(la); l.style.transform = `translateY(${(1 - la) * 8}px)`; l.querySelector('span').textContent = lt; l.querySelector('small').textContent = ls; }
  }, [DT, y, cur.x, cur.y, ripT, labA, lab.text, lab.sub]);
  if (!process.env.DRY) await p.screenshot({ path: `${out}/f${String(f).padStart(5, '0')}.jpg`, type: 'jpeg', quality: 92 });
  frame++;
}
const frames = (sec) => Math.max(1, Math.round(sec * FPS));
const docY = (sel, off = 110) => p.evaluate(([s, o]) => { const el = typeof s === 'string' ? document.querySelector(s) : null; if (!el) return null; return Math.max(0, Math.min(el.getBoundingClientRect().top + scrollY - o, document.documentElement.scrollHeight - innerHeight)); }, [sel, off]);
const maxY = () => p.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollHeight - innerHeight);
async function ready() {
  await p.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  await p.evaluate(OVERLAY);
  await p.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
  // CSS animations began on the real clock while the page loaded; start them again so the
  // recording shows the page exactly as a visitor first sees it (e.g. the headline typing)
  await p.evaluate(() => document.getAnimations().forEach((a) => { if (!a.timeline || a.timeline === document.timeline) { a.cancel(); a.play(); } }));
  y = await p.evaluate(() => scrollY);
}

/* wait for a condition while the virtual clock ticks (React's timers need it), recording nothing */
async function settle(fn, arg) {
  for (let i = 0; i < 600; i++) {
    if (await p.evaluate(fn, arg)) { await p.waitForLoadState('networkidle'); await p.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready); return; }
    await p.evaluate(() => window.__idle(16)); await p.waitForTimeout(15);
  }
  throw new Error('settle: timed out');
}

const R = {
  W: +W, H: +H,
  async open(path) { await p.goto(base + path, { waitUntil: 'networkidle' }); await ready(); await p.mouse.move(cur.x, cur.y); },
  async wait(sec) { for (let i = frames(sec); i > 0; i--) await shoot(); },
  async scrollTo(target, sec, off) {
    const y0 = y; let y1 = typeof target === 'number' ? target : target === 'bottom' ? await maxY() : await docY(target, off);
    if (y1 == null) throw new Error('no target ' + target);
    y1 = Math.min(y1, await maxY());
    const n = frames(sec); for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) { y = y0 + (y1 - y0) * ease(i / n); await shoot(); }
    y = y1;
  },
  async scrollBy(dy, sec) { await R.scrollTo(Math.max(0, y + dy), sec); },
  async move(target, sec = 0.8) {
    let to = target;
    if (typeof target === 'string') {
      to = await p.evaluate((s) => {
        let el;
        if (s.startsWith('text:')) { const [, scope, txt] = s.match(/^text:(?:(.+?)>>)?(.+)$/); const root = scope ? document.querySelector(scope) : document; el = [...root.querySelectorAll('a, button, [role=tab], summary, label, span, p, h3')].find((e) => e.textContent.trim() === txt && e.getClientRects().length); }
        else el = document.querySelector(s);
        if (!el) return null; const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); return { x: r.left + Math.min(r.width / 2, 120), y: r.top + r.height / 2 };
      }, target);
      if (!to) throw new Error('no element ' + target);
    }
    const a = { ...cur }, n = frames(sec);
    for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) { const k = ease(i / n); cur = { x: a.x + (to.x - a.x) * k, y: a.y + (to.y - a.y) * k }; await p.mouse.move(cur.x, cur.y); await shoot(); }
  },
  async click(hold = 0.5) { rip = frame; await p.mouse.down(); await p.mouse.up(); await R.wait(hold); },
  async clickOn(target, sec = 0.8, hold = 0.6) { await R.move(target, sec); await R.click(hold); },
  /* client-side navigation (what a click on an in-app link does) */
  async nav(path, hold = 0) {
    await p.evaluate((u) => { history.pushState({}, '', u); dispatchEvent(new PopStateEvent('popstate')); }, path);
    await settle((u) => location.pathname === u.split('?')[0] && !!document.querySelector('.page-in'), path);
    y = await p.evaluate(() => scrollY);
    if (hold) await R.wait(hold);
  },
  async afterClickNav(hold = 0) { await settle(() => !!document.querySelector('.page-in')); y = await p.evaluate(() => scrollY); if (hold) await R.wait(hold); },
  async type(text, cps = 12) { for (const ch of text) { await p.keyboard.type(ch); await R.wait(1 / cps); } },
  async key(k, hold = 0.4) { await p.keyboard.press(k); await R.wait(hold); },
  label(text, sub = '', sec = 3.2) { lab = { text, sub, at: frame, until: frame + frames(sec) }; chapters.push({ t: frame / FPS, text, sub }); },
  syncY: async () => { y = await p.evaluate(() => scrollY); },
  page: p,
};

const t0 = Date.now();
await SEGMENTS[name](R);
writeFileSync(`${out}/chapters.json`, JSON.stringify({ frames: frame, fps: FPS, chapters }, null, 1));
console.log(`${name}: ${frame} frames (${(frame / FPS).toFixed(1)} s) in ${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(0)} s`, errs.length ? errs.slice(0, 4) : '');
await b.close();

/* The walkthrough, as segments. Each starts from a fresh page load so it can be
   recorded (and re-recorded) on its own; make-video.sh joins them in ORDER.
   `phone` and `tablet` are recorded at their own sizes and shown side by side. */
export const ORDER = ['home', 'zenstra', 'adapid', 'botshield', 'icms', 'company', 'research', 'contact', 'dark', 'devices'];

const NAV = 'nav[aria-label="Primary"]';
const tab = (list, n) => `[role=tablist][aria-label="${list}"] [role=tab]:nth-of-type(${n})`;

/* Scroll through a page, stopping at each selector for `hold` seconds. */
async function tour(R, stops) {
  for (const [sel, hold = 1.6, off] of stops) {
    const to = sel === 'bottom' ? 'bottom' : sel;
    const y0 = await R.page.evaluate(() => scrollY);
    const y1 = to === 'bottom' ? await R.page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollHeight - innerHeight)
      : await R.page.evaluate(([s, o]) => { const el = document.querySelector(s); return el ? el.getBoundingClientRect().top + scrollY - o : null; }, [to, off ?? 110]);
    if (y1 == null) throw new Error('tour: no ' + sel);
    const d = Math.abs(y1 - y0);
    await R.scrollTo(to, Math.min(2.6, Math.max(0.9, d / 1100)), off);
    await R.wait(hold);
  }
}
